title: Are Europe’s extreme summers the new normal? What the science says
facts: Temperatures reached 40 degrees Celsius across Germany, the Czech Republic, and Poland in late June 2026.
One town in France recorded a peak temperature of 44 degrees Celsius during the early-summer heatwave.
An early-summer heatwave in France caused an estimated 1,000 excess deaths.
World Weather Attribution reported 2,300 climate-related deaths in 12 European countries during the 2025 summer heatwave.
World Weather Attribution determined extreme heatwaves of this magnitude are tens to hundreds of times more likely than in 2003.
Heat-related deaths in Europe have risen by an average of 52 per million people annually since the 1990s.
Dr Hans Kluge serves as the World Health Organization’s regional director for Europe.
June heatwaves in Europe were approximately 3.5 degrees Celsius cooler in 1976 compared to present levels.
Europe has warmed at approximately twice the global average rate since the 1980s.
Dr Akshay Deoras is a climate scientist at the University of Reading.
Stalled high-pressure systems known as heat domes act as immediate triggers for concentrated European heatwaves.
Professor Hannah Cloke is a hydrologist and climate researcher at the University of Reading.
Copernicus reported that over 95% of Europe experienced above-average temperatures in 2025.
The Lancet Countdown Europe calculated that 62,000 heat-related deaths occurred across Europe in 2024.
Dr Hans Kluge urged European governments to manage heatwaves using permanent infrastructure similar to winter flu planning.
